summary: Defines managed objects describing the behavior of an SNMP entity itself, as a Management Information Base module. It covers system-level information and SNMP statistics so a manager can query how an agent is doing. It replaces RFC 1907, the MIB for SNMPv2.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3418 defines standard SNMP objects that describe an SNMP entity, including its name, uptime, supported MIB modules, message counters, and notifications. An SNMP manager can use these objects to inspect the entity and its management service.

subtitle: The MIB objects that describe an SNMP entity's identity, supported modules, counters, and notifications.

tldr.problem: An SNMP manager needs standard objects for learning about an SNMP entity and checking the behavior of its management service.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3418 defines the SNMPv2-MIB module, including system information, SNMP counters, notification identifiers, well-known traps, and a coordination object for SET operations.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3418 is Internet Standard STD 62 and obsoletes RFC 1907. It defines current objects alongside older counters marked obsolete.

today: RFC 3418 is an Internet Standard (STD 62) and obsoletes RFC 1907. The batch metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 3418.

sections.title: A MIB for the SNMP Entity
sections.content:
SNMP managed objects are accessed through a virtual information store called the Management Information Base (MIB). RFC 3418 defines objects that describe the behavior of an SNMP entity, using the Structure of Management Information version 2 (SMIv2).

The module is named SNMPv2-MIB. It builds on the SNMP architecture and the SMIv2 definitions cited by the RFC, and replaces the earlier MIB specification in RFC 1907.
sections.plainLanguage: This MIB is a standard set of questions an SNMP manager can ask about the SNMP service itself. It describes the entity, the modules it supports, and selected activity.

sections.title: The System Group
sections.content:
The system group at { mib-2 1 } contains objects common to managed systems. sysDescr describes the entity; sysObjectID identifies its network-management subsystem; and sysUpTime reports how long the network-management portion has run since its last reinitialization.

sysContact, sysName, and sysLocation hold administrative text. sysServices indicates which protocol layers the entity may serve. The related sysORTable lists MIB-module capabilities of the local command responder, while sysORLastChange records when an entry last changed.
sections.plainLanguage: The system group records a device description, identifier, uptime, contact, name, location, and service layers. A separate table lists the MIB modules the command responder supports.

sections.title: SNMP Counters and Control
sections.content:
The snmp group at { mib-2 11 } provides counters and control objects. Examples include snmpInPkts for messages delivered from the transport service, snmpInBadVersions for unsupported SNMP versions, and snmpInASNParseErrs for ASN.1 or BER decoding errors.

snmpSilentDrops counts confirmed-class PDUs dropped because a response with empty variable bindings would still exceed a size limit. snmpProxyDrops counts confirmed-class PDUs dropped when forwarding to a proxy target fails in a way that leaves no response to return. The module retains several RFC 1213 counters with status obsolete.
sections.plainLanguage: The SNMP group keeps counts of incoming messages, unsupported versions, decoding errors, and some dropped requests. Some older counters remain named in the module but are marked obsolete.

sections.title: Notifications and Coordinated Changes
sections.content:
snmpTrapOID identifies the notification being sent and appears as the second variable binding in every SNMPv2-Trap-PDU and InformRequest-PDU. snmpTrapEnterprise identifies the enterprise associated with a trap and is used when a proxy maps an older Trap-PDU into an SNMPv2 trap.

The module defines coldStart for reinitialization where configuration may have changed, warmStart for reinitialization with configuration unaltered, and authenticationFailure for receipt of a message that was not properly authenticated. snmpSetSerialNo is an advisory lock for command generators coordinating SET operations.
sections.plainLanguage: Notifications carry an identifier for the event being reported. The MIB names restart and authentication-failure notifications, and it provides a lock that cooperating managers can use before changing values.

sections.title: Which Objects an Entity Supports
sections.content:
The RFC groups objects into conformance units, including the system group, core SNMP group, community counters, SET coordination, and notification groups. Its current compliance statement is snmpBasicComplianceRev2.

Rev2 requires the core SNMP group, SET group, system group, and basic notification group. The community group is required for entities that support community-based authentication. The warm-start group is required when an entity supports command responders and can reinitialize without changing its configuration. The earlier snmpBasicCompliance statement is deprecated and replaced by Rev2.
sections.plainLanguage: The conformance statement lists which object groups an SNMP entity must provide. Some groups are required only when the entity supports particular authentication or restart behavior.

sections.title: Protecting Read-Write Objects
sections.content:
Some objects have read-write access and may be sensitive or vulnerable in a network environment. Allowing SET operations without proper protection can harm network operations. The RFC says SNMPv1 by itself is not secure, and a secure network alone does not control who may read or change these objects.

The RFC recommends considering SNMPv3 security features: the User-based Security Model and the View-based Access Control Model. The customer or user is responsible for configuring access so that only principals with legitimate rights can GET or SET these objects.
sections.plainLanguage: Some MIB values can be changed, so access to them needs protection. Configure permissions so only authorized users can read or change those values.
